_readme: Per-country weight on how prominently the trip planner SUGGESTS a city.
Default is 1. This only reorders discovery surfaces — the city picker's
default list and ties between equally-good destinations. It NEVER filters:
every route stays searchable, stays on the map, keeps its /connections page,
and is returned in full when a plan asks for it. Typing 'Lviv' still puts
Lviv first. tests/verify-plan.mjs pins that distinction.
scope says where a weight applies:
'always' — everywhere, including the region-filtered 'start from' chips.
'global' — only where cities from every continent compete in one list.
Since the chips gained Europe/Asia/North America tabs, a whole continent no
longer needs damping there: the tab already says which product you want, and
damping inside a tab would make the visible train counts stop descending.

UA.reason: Ukraine is at war. Ukrainian Railways runs these trains and the data is accurate, but heading a leisure trip planner with 'start from Kyiv' is the wrong default. Still fully searchable and routable.

CN.reason: China Railway sleepers are in the dataset but are not the European night-train market this site serves; Chengdu as a suggested starting point is noise for almost every visitor.

US.reason: Amtrak — same reason as CN: real data, wrong market for a European hub list.

CA.reason: VIA Rail — same reason as US.

JP.reason: JR West's Sunrise Izumo / Seto — same reason as CN: real data, wrong market for a European hub list. Leads the Asia tab on its own merits.

TH.reason: State Railway of Thailand — same reason as JP: real data, wrong market for a European hub list. Leads the Asia tab on its own merits.

VN.reason: Vietnam Railways — same reason as TH: real data, wrong market for a European hub list. Competes in the Asia tab on its own merits.

GE.reason: Caucasus: real rail, peripheral to the European corridors this site sells.
